scope: Independent original-resolution pixel/source review of four illustrative acts of care in Matthew25:35-36. No import, diagnosis, biography or miracle claim.

entries.alt: A woman offers a clay cup to a seated man, with a loaf of bread beside him and a water jug near her other hand.
entries.caption: A cup passes between two people while bread rests within reach. This illustration recalls the food and drink Jesus names among acts of care for another person's need.
findings: Cup exchange is anatomically plausible: woman wraps fingers around side while seated man supports base/side, both wrists attach naturally. Other hands rest plausibly at jug and knee.
Faces clearly distinct, mutually attentive eyes and restrained smiles fit kindness. Natural skin, hair, cloth and courtyard light; no Christ likeness or halo.
Bread is visible without inventing consumption; cup contents and water purity not visually established. Caption describes offered drink and illustrative care, not named historical event.
conditions: Keep scene framed as illustration of the care Jesus names, not a named recorded historical event or literal depiction of Christ.

entries.alt: An older man and a woman hold a folded woolen covering between them at an open doorway.
entries.caption: At an open doorway, a folded covering is offered with a warm welcome. The scene illustrates the hospitality and clothing Jesus remembers in His teaching about caring for others.
findings: Folded textile is supported coherently by both people; hands remain distinct with natural grip and occlusion, no fused fabric/fingers.
Older man and younger adult woman clearly distinct, mutual eye contact and warmth without camera posing. Doorway and interior light are photographic.
Covering and welcome plausibly illustrate Matthew25:35-36. Caption does not identify homelessness, kinship, exact fabric provenance or outcome.
conditions: Keep scene framed as illustration of the care Jesus names, not a named recorded historical event or literal depiction of Christ.

entries.alt: A seated visitor holds the hand of a reclining woman as they look toward one another beside a small table with a cup and bowl.
entries.caption: A visitor sits close and holds the hand of a woman resting in bed. This imagined moment of companionship reflects Jesus' invitation to visit those who are sick.
findings: Visitor two hands surround one resting hand coherently; the reclining arm follows a plausible wrist/hand path and folds do not create extra limbs.
Women have different face shapes/hair/age cues and attentive reciprocal gaze. Natural quiet concern, no theatrical distress or healing gesture.
Bed, cup and bowl are ordinary setting objects; no diagnosis, relationship or recovery inferred. Caption explicitly imagined visit, not a miracle or named encounter.
conditions: Keep scene framed as illustration of the care Jesus names, not a named recorded historical event or literal depiction of Christ.

entries.alt: Two men sit facing one another in a stone room beside a barred wooden doorway, leaning into an attentive conversation.
entries.caption: A visitor gives his attention to a man seated in confinement. This illustration recalls Jesus' words about visiting a prisoner and seeing a person others may overlook.
findings: Both men have distinct hair/face shapes and mutually directed attention; natural soft expressions suit a meaningful visit.
Clasped left hands and visitor resting hand anatomically coherent; legs, clothing and seats physically plausible.
Bars and masonry support confinement setting without claims about exact prison architecture, reason for detention, guilt, innocence or impending release. No Christ likeness or miraculous escape.
conditions: Keep scene framed as illustration of the care Jesus names, not a named recorded historical event or literal depiction of Christ.
